question: After the pacing defect is fixed, should outbound recovery keep ambiguous entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed?
rationale: Tests can prove either behavior, but the choice affects upgrade/operator semantics: pending preserves future recovery, while terminal failed gives operators a clearer fail-closed state until the broader delivery ledger exists.

options.title: Fix Pacing And Accept Pending
options.body: Require the no-op deferral repair first, then merge if maintainers want ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the broader delivery-ledger design is ready.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a companion doctor, UI, or API path before changing ambiguous entries to remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Fix Pacing And Accept Pending
recommendation.body: Require the no-op deferral repair first, then merge if maintainers want ambiguous rows to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses SQLite queue state, recovery behavior, and operator expectations, and this owner appears in the delivery-queue migration history.
